title: Bit Manipulation Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on binary representation, bitwise operators and shifts, two's complement, and the core bit tricks: checking/setting bits, x & (x-1), single number via XOR, counting bits, and subset enumeration with bitmasks.

chapters.title: Bits and Binary Representation
points: Bit i has weight 2^i, counted from 0 at the right (LSB); an n-bit number holds 0 to 2^n - 1 unsigned
Convert decimal to binary by repeated division by 2 (read remainders bottom-up): 13 = 1101
Mental model: an integer is a row of on/off switches, and bit tricks flip those switches directly instead of using arithmetic
Hex groups 4 bits per digit (0xF = 1111), which makes masks like 0xFF and 0x80000000 easy to read
Language literals: 0b1101 (Python, C++14, Java 7), 0x for hex; bin(x) in Python, Integer.toBinaryString in Java

chapters.title: Operators: AND, OR, XOR, NOT and Shifts
points: AND (&) gives 1 only if both bits are 1: use it to mask or test bits; x & 0 = 0, x & x = x
OR (|) gives 1 if either bit is 1: use it to set bits; x | 0 = x
XOR (^) gives 1 if the bits differ: x ^ x = 0, x ^ 0 = x, and it is commutative and associative
NOT (~) flips every bit, so ~x = -x - 1; in Python it yields negative numbers and needs a mask like & 0xFF
Left shift x << k multiplies by 2^k; right shift x >> k floors division by 2^k, and >>> (Java/JS) fills zeros while >> keeps the sign bit

chapters.title: Two's Complement and Negative Numbers
points: Two's complement: -x = ~x + 1; the top bit has weight -2^(n-1), so in 8 bits 1111 1111 = -1
n-bit signed range is -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1) - 1, so there is one more negative than positive value (abs(INT_MIN) overflows)
Addition and subtraction use the same hardware for signed and unsigned values, which is why this encoding is used
x & -x isolates the lowest set bit, because -x flips everything above that bit and keeps it
Gotcha: Python ints are unbounded, so negatives need & 0xFFFFFFFF to emulate 32 bits; left-shifting a signed int into the sign bit is undefined in C/C++

chapters.title: Check, Set, Clear, Toggle and x & (x-1)
points: Check bit i: (x >> i) & 1 or x & (1 << i) != 0
Set bit i: x | (1 << i); clear bit i: x & ~(1 << i); toggle bit i: x ^ (1 << i)
x & (x-1) clears the lowest set bit, because x-1 flips the lowest 1 and all zeros below it
Power of two test: x > 0 && (x & (x-1)) == 0, since a power of two has exactly one set bit
Mistake: precedence, so write (x & 1) == 0, since == binds tighter than & in C, C++, Java; and use 1L << i for i >= 31 to avoid int overflow

chapters.title: XOR Tricks, Counting Bits and Bitmask Subsets
points: Single number: XOR all elements, since pairs cancel (x ^ x = 0) and the lone value remains in O(n) time and O(1) space
Swap without a temp: a ^= b; b ^= a; a ^= b (breaks if both names refer to the same variable)
Count set bits (Kernighan): loop x &= x - 1 and count iterations, which runs once per set bit; builtins are popcount, bit_count(), Integer.bitCount
Count bits for 0..n by DP: bits[i] = bits[i >> 1] + (i & 1), or bits[i] = bits[i & (i-1)] + 1, in O(n)
Subsets of n items: loop mask from 0 to (1 << n) - 1 and include item i when mask & (1 << i); this gives 2^n subsets, practical for n up to about 20

chapters.title: Bit Manipulation Cheat Sheet
points: Operators: & mask/test, | set, ^ toggle/cancel, ~ flip, << multiply by 2^k, >> divide by 2^k
Bit i: check (x>>i)&1, set x|(1<<i), clear x&~(1<<i), toggle x^(1<<i)
Tricks: x&(x-1) clears the lowest set bit, x&-x isolates it, -x = ~x+1, power of two is x>0 && !(x&(x-1))
XOR identities: x^x=0, x^0=x; single number is a fold of XOR; Kernighan counts bits in O(set bits)
Subsets: for mask in 0..2^n-1, test bit i; mind precedence, 1L for 64-bit, and masking in Python
